tier_reason: First-party README charts (CPS.png, CPS_Reuseport.png, RPS.png, Bandwidth.png) compare Nginx on the Linux kernel stack (epoll) against Nginx+F-Stack, with hardware stated (Xeon E5-2670 v3, XL710 40GbE, CentOS 7.2, kernel 3.10.104). Compiler, flags, load generator and client setup are not stated and no benchmark scripts or configs for the kernel comparison are published, so it cannot be A; no peer-reviewed or independent suite was found, so C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README 'Nginx Testing Result' charts. Bandwidth values are the printed data labels; RPS/CPS values are approximate, read off the right axis of the chart images. CPS (Connection: close, 600-byte body, 1-20 cores): Nginx+F-Stack 5.82 Gbit/s (~1.04M CPS) vs Nginx 'si' (kernel, IRQ smp_affinity spread, no reuseport) 0.47 Gbit/s (~86k CPS) at 20 cores, ~12x (derived from page data). CPS_Reuseport (Connection: close, different test environment, 1-16 cores): F-Stack 5.78 Gbit/s (~1.02M CPS) vs Nginx+reuseport 2.47 (~0.44M) vs default Nginx 0.63 (~0.11M) at 16 cores, ~2.3x vs reuseport (derived from page data). RPS (keep-alive, 600-byte body, 1-24 cores): F-Stack 26.96 Gbit/s (~4.77M RPS) vs Nginx si 18.49 (~3.27M) vs default Nginx 2.11 (~0.38M) at 24 cores, ~1.46x vs the tuned kernel and ~12.8x vs the default config (derived from page data). Bandwidth (keep-alive, 3.7 KB body, 1-16 cores): F-Stack leads at low core counts (4.30 vs 2.90 Gbit/s at 1 core, 33.75 vs 23.28 at 8 cores, ~1.45x derived from page data), but both hit the ~37.1 Gbit/s 40GbE ceiling at 16 cores (parity). The README headline '10 million concurrent connections, 5 million RPS, 1 million CPS' under full NIC load: the 5M RPS and 1M CPS figures roughly match the charts, while the 10M-connection figure has no supporting chart.
corrections.workload: Nginx serving a fixed body. CPS (Connection: close, 600-byte body), RPS (keep-alive, 600-byte body) and bandwidth (keep-alive, 3.7 KB body) on 1-24 physical cores. Kernel Nginx (Linux default config with all softirqs on core 0; 'si' = per-IRQ smp_affinity spread; 'Reuseport' = reuseport in nginx.conf) vs Nginx+F-Stack (DPDK kernel bypass plus a ported FreeBSD TCP/IP stack; body returned directly from nginx.conf). Intel XL710 40GbE NIC.
corrections.hardware: Intel XL710 40GbE QSFP+ NIC, Intel Xeon E5-2670 v3 @ 2.30GHz (NUMA), 128GB RAM, CentOS 7.2, kernel 3.10.104-1-tlinux2 (the CPS_Reuseport chart was run in a different, unstated environment)
corrections.license: BSD-2-Clause for F-Stack's main code, per the LICENSE file (GitHub reports 'Other'/NOASSERTION). Bundled components: DPDK BSD-3-Clause (kernel modules GPL-2.0), FreeBSD stack BSD-4-Clause, Nginx BSD-2-Clause, Redis BSD-3-Clause, libplebnet/libuinet BSD-2-Clause, inih BSD-3-Clause, Microthread framework GPL-2.0.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 4,265 stars. Used in production at Tencent Cloud (DNSPod authoritative DNS, HttpDNS (D+), COS access module, CDN access module), per the README.
corrections.caveats: Numbers exist only in chart images. Bandwidth data labels are readable, but RPS/CPS values are approximate reads off the chart axis. The ~12x ratios are against untuned or IRQ-only-tuned kernel Nginx. Against the best-tuned kernel config the gain is ~1.46x RPS (keep-alive, 24 cores) and ~2.3x CPS (vs reuseport, 16 cores), and 3.7 KB-body bandwidth reaches parity at 40GbE line rate. Compiler, flags, load generator and client setup are not stated, and no benchmark scripts are published. Hardware and kernel (E5-2670 v3, kernel 3.10) are 2016-era. The CPS_Reuseport chart ran in a different environment. The page does not say whether kernel Nginx also returned the body directly from nginx.conf. F-Stack is not a drop-in epoll replacement: it needs DPDK NIC takeover, hugepages and dedicated busy-polling cores, and the LD_PRELOAD adapter uses ~2x CPU (per adapter/syscall/README.md). The '10M concurrent connections' claim has no supporting data. docs/F-Stack_Architecture_Layer1_System_Overview.md claims '5M RPS vs kernel 200K RPS, 25x' without a source, and the README RPS chart contradicts it (kernel Nginx si ~3.27M RPS). BSD-4-Clause and GPL-2.0 components are bundled.

notes: The charts could be read once downloaded (bandwidth data labels exact, RPS/CPS read off the axis), so claimed_speedup is filled in. The headline ~12x holds only against untuned or IRQ-tuned kernel Nginx; against tuned kernel configs the win is ~1.5-2.3x, with bandwidth parity at line rate. Supporting first-party data: adapter/syscall/README.md LD_PRELOAD charts, and the Photon wiki single-thread echo test (25G NIC, 512 B), which shows +20% ping-pong (1.23 vs 1.03 Gb/s) and +40% streaming (3.74 vs 2.60 Gb/s) vs Linux 6.x kernel sockets. last_commit is taken from default branch dev: release/2.0 has a commit on 2026-09-24, and no commit is dated 2026-09-25. Usability stays 'mixed' (BSD-2-Clause core plus non-OSI BSD-4-Clause and GPL-2.0 parts). No independent or peer-reviewed benchmark was searched for because the WebSearch budget is exhausted.
